messages:
Priya Varma: Heads-up — noticed a potential permission-gating regression in the Console after yesterday's role-matrix refactor. A user with \"viewer\" role saw the project edit button for a specific project. Repro steps below.

Priya Varma: Repro steps: 1) Login as user with viewer role on org X 2) Navigate to Projects > My Project 3) Observe top-right shows \"Edit Project\" button and modal opens.

Priya Varma: Logs from the browser console and API trace:
```
GET /api/v1/projects/123/permissions => 200 { roles: [\"viewer\"], perms: [\"view\"] }
UI computed can_edit = permissions.includes('edit') || role === 'editor' || role === 'admin' // returns true unexpectedly
```

Alex Chen: omg, thanks for flagging. Can you paste the network trace (server-side) and the exact user id? I want to confirm whether the backend returned extra perms or if the front-end logic is wrong.

Priya Varma: user id u-0a1b2c3d, attached server response below (sanitized):
```
{ \"user\": \"u-0a1b2c3d\", \"roles\": [\"viewer\"], \"computed_permissions\": [\"view\"] }
```

Tess Nguyen: pinging @Priya @Alex — likely a frontend gating bug. I pushed a quick local repro and the UI uses a helper that caches role -> permission mapping. After the refactor, default map for unknown role keys returns {edit: true} because of a typo. Will link PR in a sec.

Tess Nguyen: found the offending code: 
```js
const DEFAULT_ROLE_MAP = { viewer: {view:true}, editor: {view:true, edit:true} }
// bug: fallback was set to DEFAULT_ROLE_MAP['editor'] instead of null
const permMap = ROLE_MAP[role] || DEFAULT_ROLE_MAP['editor']
```

Sam Ortiz: if this is true for prod we should treat as P1 until we know scope. How many users affected? Any customer-facing impact?

Priya Varma: Initial check: only projects with legacy role bindings that hit the old path. Estimate ~22 internal users + 3 customers flagged via support ticket #SUP-1289. Not widespread, but customer-facing.

Alex Chen: OK let's triage: 1) Tess to hotfix UI fallback 2) Run audit log query for permission-change events / KMS access (to rule out tampering) 3) Backfill Which users saw Edit and rollback if necessary.

kms-bot: KMS audit snippet for project key pk-987:
```
2026-03-19T18:12:01Z GET /kms/keys/pk-987/access granted to service:redwood-console -> principal:svc-ui-renderer
2026-03-19T18:12:01Z DECRYPT request by svc-ui-renderer - result: SUCCESS
```

Priya Varma: Good to know; no suspicious key rotates or unauthorized key usage. This looks like purely a client-side gating problem, but still want to confirm backend didn't emit edit perms.

Alex Chen: @Tess can you open a PR and also put a temporary server-side defense that denies edit action unless backend returns explicit edit permission? Prefer layered defense.

Tess Nguyen: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/8772 — adds server-side check and fixes fallback. Will also add a feature-flag to disable the new role-map until we validate.

security-bot: Created incident INC-2026-45 and attached initial notes + affected customer list. See https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-2026-45

Sam Ortiz: Good. @Alex let's decide rollback vs hotfix. I prefer hotfix + canary rollback if anything looks off. Can we deploy to canary and run smoke?

Tess Nguyen: Starting canary deploy now. Deploy command: `./deploy canary console-ui --tag hotfix-8772`.

deploy-bot: deploy started by Tess Nguyen: console-ui hotfix-8772 -> canary (region-us-east-1)

deploy-bot: canary deploy successful: 3/3 pods healthy. Running smoke tests.

deploy-bot: smoke tests: all green. No errors in 60s window.

Alex Chen: Run the audit query for UI permission exposure (tools/queries/permission_exposure.sql) against last 48h and share results here. Prioritize projects with legacy bindings.

Priya Varma: Audit query results: 25 unique users saw edit button; 3 are customer accounts (cust-a, cust-b, cust-c). Logged actions: only one attempted save (failed due to backend guard) so no unauthorized modifications recorded.

Alex Chen: Good — no write operations succeeded. Next steps: 1) Patch merged to main 2) Backfill and notify affected customers + SOC and legal per policy 3) Add alert for any future UI-perm/front-end mismatch 4) Add unit tests covering role fallback.

Priya Varma: I'll draft the customer notification and notify support/success. Will also add a KMS audit periodic check to the runbook to ensure we're not missing key misuse.

Tess Nguyen: Patch merged and deployed to prod. PR link and changelog: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/8772/merged

security-bot: Incident INC-2026-45 updated: severity downgraded to S2 after fix; remediation actions recorded.

Priya Varma: Thanks everyone. Closing thread after final postmortem write-up.

Alex Chen: Good catch, Priya. Great cross-team response. :thumbsup:
